verdict.rationale: MX documents registrable webhooks that send HTTPS POST callbacks to a URL you choose for subscribed events, and the Client Dashboard lets you create, edit, test and delete them, so push-based updates exist. The evidence does not show signatures or name the specific event types the story asks for. Missing for 10: webhook signature verification, documented event types for new transactions, balance updates and connection state changes, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, data changes arrive as signed webhooks — new transactions, balance updates, connection state changes — so my system stays current without polling

citations.quote: MX provides webhooks that send HTTPS POST callback requests to the URL of your choice. This enables you to subscribe to certain events
Client Dashboard makes it easy to create, edit, test, and delete the webhooks that are available for your integration.
